items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: He knew this lady, Catherine Rank, that played in the pit. And she showed me a boogie- woogie pattern on the piano so I started playing.

ctx.x: Well when you started out, was there a bit of a boogie-woogie craze when you were a kid, playing piano?

I would think so. That’s how I got influenced. I saw a little kid, Sugar Chile Robinson with the Basie Band. My parents used to take me to stage shows at the Albee and the Shubert Theater in Cincinnati. So there’s be a show like Blackstone the Magician, the Count Basie Band, and he had Sugar Chile Robinson. And I fell in love with boogie- woogie watching that kid play. I was three years old. So I came home and started to pick it out on the piano. And my dad was a professional, or semi-professional bass player. He…
Was it hard for you to stick to the page when you were learning classical music? Because you had already done a little bit sort of by ear?
